options.text: Firms enter, market supply decreases, and the price rises until profits are zero.
options.why: Moves the supply curve the wrong direction when firms enter.

options.text: Firms enter, market supply increases, the price falls, and economic profit returns to zero.
options.why: Positive economic profit attracts entry, which shifts market supply right, lowers the price, and pushes profit to zero.

options.text: Firms exit, market supply decreases, the price rises, and economic profit returns to zero.
options.why: Reverses the direction of entry and exit.

options.text: Firms enter, market demand increases, the price rises, and profits grow.
options.why: Treats entry as a demand-side change.

options.text: No firms enter because barriers to entry are low only in the long run.
options.why: Confuses long-run adjustment with barriers to entry.
